cases.q: (Not a text from them. Your background job reported back to you; nothing from it has reached them yet.) Before it, they asked: what's the difference between my HSA and my FSA? which one do I use for the dentist bill?

report.title: HSA vs FSA for the dentist bill
texts: HSA: health savings account, linked to the high-deductible plan, money rolls over year to year and is theirs. FSA: flexible spending account through the employer, use-it-or-lose-it by March 15; balance $410. Dentist bill $380 qualifies for both. Suggest FSA since that money expires. Sources on the page: https://context.lc/p/@kit/projects/hsa-vs-fsa.page.md

cases.reply: Both pay for medical stuff, but they work differently. Your HSA is your own savings account tied to your health plan, and whatever you don't spend stays yours. Your FSA comes through work and anything left on March 15 is gone, and you have $410 in it. So pay the $380 dentist bill from the FSA. Sources: https://context.lc/p/@kit/projects/hsa-vs-fsa.page.md
